final_candidates.decision_summary: RING zinc-coordinating cysteine; classic pathogenic substitution that disrupts BRCA1-BARD1 E3 ligase activity and homologous recombination while the domain remains expressed and largely folded.
Well-characterized BRCT pathogenic variant that abolishes phospho-peptide binding and DNA repair; protein is expressed with only modest stability loss.
Conserved BRCT residue; introducing charge disrupts the function-critical pocket and phospho-recognition, a known pathogenic class with retained overall domain architecture.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 dominated by established loss-of-function variants; no external evidence available and self-iteration would not change ranking.

history.rationale: Classic pathogenic RING-domain mutation disrupting the zinc-coordinating C3HC4 finger; abolishes E3 ligase activity and BARD1 interaction while the RING fold is only locally perturbed.
RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine; known pathogenic mutation class that disrupts BRCA1-BARD1 ubiquitin ligase activity while the domain largely retains fold context.
Second zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING finger; similar loss-of-function mechanism as C61G, disrupting BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimer function.
Second zinc-coordinating cysteine in RING; strong loss-of-function but slightly higher unfolding risk than C61G.
Well-characterized pathogenic BRCT mutation disrupting the phosphopeptide-binding groove and BRCA1 transcriptional/DNA-damage-response function.
Classic BRCT-domain pathogenic variant that abolishes phospho-peptide binding and DNA repair while remaining expressed and largely folded.
Pathogenic C-terminal BRCT mutation that impairs phospho-ligand binding and tumor-suppressor function.
Conserved BRCT hydrophobic-core residue; charge introduction disrupts function-critical pocket, known pathogenic class.
Pathogenic BRCT repeat 1 mutation abolishing phosphorylated-protein recognition essential for DNA repair.
BRCT mutation known to impair phospho-binding; bulky Phe may perturb local packing more than needed, so demoted slightly.
Pathogenic BRCT mutation disrupting the hydrophobic core of the BRCT interface, compromising ligand binding.
BRCT2 proline important for domain architecture; substitution disrupts BRCT repeat interface function.
RING-domain residue at the BARD1 interaction surface; charge loss impairs heterodimer stability and E3 activity.
RING-domain surface residue affecting E2 interaction; milder but likely retains fold well.
BRCT surface lysine implicated in phosphopeptide recognition; charge reversal impairs binding without gross unfolding.
Weakest candidate; redundant with stronger BRCT variants and less certain functional impact.

rejection.reason: Weakest candidate; redundant with stronger BRCT variants and less certain functional impact.
